forces.title: Global payments revenue growth moderating structurally
forces.description: The global payments sector is experiencing a structural transition, with revenue growth moderating from 9% to 4% annually. This shift means that future growth for Diversified Financial Conglomerates with payment activities will depend less on broad market momentum and more on deliberate competitive advantages such as operational discipline, pricing sophistication, and technological leadership, necessitating a strategic re-evaluation of business models.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Shift from Net Interest Income to fee-based revenue
forces.description: As interest rate tailwinds soften, global payments revenue is shifting from 46% Net Interest Income (NII) in 2025 to 44% NII by 2030, with fee income gaining share. This presents a headwind for Diversified Financial Conglomerates, especially those with significant banking operations, as it dampens net interest margins. They must adapt by placing greater emphasis on fee resilience, yield discipline, and monetizing value-added services alongside baseline processing.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: EMEA payments market faces margin compression and slow growth
forces.description: The payments market in Europe (as part of EMEA) is experiencing margin compression due to lower interest rates, causing treasury and deposit margins to shrink. Growth is projected to slow to about 3% annually (2025–30) from 14% (2020–25). Diversified Financial Conglomerates operating in Europe face increased pressure to rapidly shift to fee-based structures and enhance operational efficiency to counteract the dampening effect on net interest income and overall revenue growth.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Agentic AI threatens deposit NII and consumer credit card revenues
forces.description: Autonomous software agents, driven by AI, pose a significant risk to Diversified Financial Conglomerates by optimizing account yields and dynamically routing transactions. This could put an estimated $75 billion in global payments revenue at risk by 2030, primarily impacting deposit Net Interest Income (NII) through cash sweeps to higher-yielding accounts ($65 billion at risk) and consumer credit card revenues ($10 billion at risk) through rail substitution and fee avoidance.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Stablecoins bypass traditional payments, impacting DFC revenues
forces.description: The scaling of digital assets like stablecoins and tokenized deposits poses an additional headwind for Diversified Financial Conglomerates. These digital assets bypass traditional interchange and foreign-exchange (FX) conversion markups, and shift float income out of commercial bank deposits. This directly pressures margins on foreign-exchange spreads and correspondent banking fees, challenging traditional revenue streams for DFCs with these financial service offerings.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Value shifting to invisible 'control layer' in payments
forces.description: The value in global payments is relocating from front-end checkout screens to an invisible 'control layer' comprising back-end trust, machine identity, consent engines, and dynamic routing protocols. For Diversified Financial Conglomerates, this structural shift means that capturing future value will depend on positioning themselves to anchor this emerging control layer, by focusing on capabilities that combine software with durable moats such as proprietary data, embedded distribution, and trusted customer relationships.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Payment infrastructure fragmenting into regional multi-rail arenas
forces.description: Contrary to theoretical models, global payment infrastructure is fragmenting regionally into multi-rail competitive arenas. European DFCs must navigate competing pressures from zero-fee domestic real-time account-to-account networks, legacy card perimeters, and wholesale stablecoin corridors for cross-border settlement. This fragmentation creates contested strategic boundaries, requiring DFCs to manage complex structural divergences in rail adoption, regulation, and economics across markets, impacting their operational efficiency and strategic investments.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Asymmetric economics driving consolidation in payments sector
forces.description: The payments industry faces structural consolidation pressure driven by a financial imbalance: IT expenditures are projected to compound at 9% annually through 2030, while global payments revenue growth moderates to 4%. This asymmetry means massive scale or direct rail control become primary defenses against margin compression for DFCs with payment operations. While consolidation is inevitable, localized national champions with strong regional client relationships are expected to survive, suggesting strategic partnerships will be crucial.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Banks uniquely positioned to underwrite agent transactions
forces.description: Diversified Financial Conglomerates that include banking institutions possess a unique advantage in the evolving agentic commerce landscape. Their existing regulatory licenses, risk expertise, and robust balance sheets position them to underwrite agent transactions, a role nonbank entrants cannot easily replicate. This provides an upside opportunity for DFCs to defend core revenue pools and capture emerging autonomous flows by issuing verifiable machine credentials, managing delegated authorization, and proactively shaping industry standards, much like traditional card issuers.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Redeploying AI productivity gains into emerging control layer
forces.description: Diversified Financial Conglomerates can achieve significant productivity gains through AI-led automation of high-volume operations like software engineering and KYC reviews. By realizing these net cost reductions (15-20% from gross 70% productivity), DFCs can strategically redeploy capital into the emerging 'control layer' of payments. This self-funded transformation allows first movers to expand return on tangible equity by up to four percentage points, transitioning from productivity tools to operating-model enablers.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Weaker mortgage lending and high interest rates dampen Belgian housing
forces.description: The Belgian housing market is facing a challenging outlook characterized by weaker mortgage production and persistently high interest rates. Mortgage lending in the first eight months of 2026 was approximately 10% lower year-over-year. For Diversified Financial Conglomerates involved in mortgage finance in Belgium, this represents a headwind, leading to reduced demand for housing loans and potential pressure on their lending portfolios. Financing conditions are expected to remain restrictive, tempering market momentum.
forces.source_title: Second-quarter resilience masks a more challenging outlook for Belgian housing

forces.title: Growing European AI application funding supports DFC innovation
forces.description: Europe is experiencing a surge in venture capital funding for AI applications, particularly in vertical, industry-specific solutions, reaching €6.8 billion in H1 2026. This growing investment in AI, coupled with Europe's strong talent pool and academic spinouts, presents an upside driver for Diversified Financial Conglomerates. It enables DFCs to access specialized AI tools and expertise, fostering innovation in their digital financial services, operational efficiency, and customer engagement, especially within regulated environments where Europe shows particular strength.
forces.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity

forces.title: Shift to specialized vertical AI applications in European enterprise
forces.description: The European technology ecosystem is undergoing a structural shift towards specialized, vertical AI applications, moving away from one-size-fits-all software. This trend is driven by the demand for deep integration into complex, highly regulated business processes. For Diversified Financial Conglomerates, this is a significant structural change as it means a growing availability of tailored AI solutions specifically designed for financial services, enabling more targeted and effective digital transformation initiatives and potentially enhancing their competitive edge in a regulated market.
forces.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity

viewpoints.title: Global payments growth moderates, demanding operational excellence from DFCs
viewpoints.description: McKinsey foresees global payments revenue growth moderating from 9% to 4% annually, signaling a structural transition. For Diversified Financial Conglomerates with payment operations, this means performance will shift from broad market momentum to deliberate competitive advantages like commercial excellence, operational discipline, and technological leadership. DFCS must prioritize fee resilience and yield discipline as interest rate tailwinds soften and AI threatens deposit yields and card fee pools.
viewpoints.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

viewpoints.title: EMEA payments face margin compression and slow growth, shifting revenue mix
viewpoints.description: The EMEA region's payments market, relevant to European DFCs, is projected to slow to about 3% annual growth in 2025–30, a sharp decline from 14% in 2020–25. Lower interest rates are compressing treasury and deposit margins, prompting a rapid shift to fee-based structures. DFCs with significant operations in EMEA will need to adapt their strategies to manage this margin compression and focus on fee-generating services as NII contributions decline.
viewpoints.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

viewpoints.title: Agentic AI poses significant revenue risk for DFCs in deposits and cards
viewpoints.description: McKinsey projects that agentic artificial intelligence could put approximately $75 billion in global payments revenue at risk by 2030, affecting retail and commercial deposits and consumer credit cards. For Diversified Financial Conglomerates, this risk primarily stems from software agents sweeping idle cash to higher-yielding accounts and optimizing card payments to minimize fees, directly challenging traditional deposit franchises and credit card economics through balance migration and yield compression.
viewpoints.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

viewpoints.title: Stablecoins present additional revenue headwinds by bypassing traditional financial rails
viewpoints.description: Digital assets like stablecoins and tokenized deposits are expected to pose an additional headwind to payments and deposit revenues for DFCs. McKinsey notes that stablecoins bypass traditional interchange and foreign-exchange (FX) conversion markups, and shift float income out of commercial bank deposits. As cross-border corporate corridors adopt tokenized settlement, DFCs with exposure to correspondent banking and FX services will face direct margin pressure, impacting their diversified revenue streams.
viewpoints.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

viewpoints.title: Durable moats critical for DFCs to capture value in evolving payments landscape
viewpoints.description: McKinsey analysis suggests that in a slower-growth, increasingly fee-led payments market, value will accrue selectively to players combining software capabilities with durable, harder-to-replicate moats. These include proprietary data, embedded distribution, trusted customer relationships, and deep workflow integration. Diversified Financial Conglomerates need to reevaluate their strategy to build and leverage these 'moats' rather than solely relying on proximity to the end-user, to secure selective value capture.
viewpoints.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

viewpoints.title: Banking institutions well-positioned to underwrite agent transactions in new era
viewpoints.description: McKinsey highlights that banking institutions, typically components of Diversified Financial Conglomerates, are uniquely positioned to underwrite agent transactions. Their regulatory licenses, risk expertise, and balance sheets are durable moats that nonbank entrants cannot easily replicate. This provides a strategic advantage for DFCs with banking arms to defend core revenue pools and capture emerging autonomous flows by issuing verifiable machine credentials, managing delegated authorization, and actively shaping industry standards for AI-driven commerce.
viewpoints.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

viewpoints.title: Belgian housing market faces challenging outlook from weaker mortgage activity
viewpoints.description: ING Think assesses a challenging outlook for the Belgian housing market despite recent resilience, with weaker mortgage production and higher interest rates signalling a loss of demand momentum. For Diversified Financial Conglomerates with mortgage lending activities in Belgium, this implies potential pressure on their housing finance portfolios, impacting growth. The persistent high interest rates and falling energy prices further affect consumer purchasing power and the attractiveness of new mortgages, leading to a cooling market.
viewpoints.source_title: Second-quarter resilience masks a more challenging outlook for Belgian housing

viewpoints.title: Europe's AI application layer strength benefits DFCs in regulated environments
viewpoints.description: McKinsey finds Europe is well-positioned for the emerging AI application layer opportunity, particularly in vertical (industry-specific) AI where deep integration into highly regulated and heterogeneous environments is key. This is positive for Diversified Financial Conglomerates, as DFIs operate in such regulated settings. The growing European AI talent pool and increasing funding for vertical AI applications mean DFCs can leverage specialized AI solutions to transform complex business processes, improve efficiency, and potentially offer new digital financial services.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity

pnl_drivers.driver: Shift from Net Interest Income (NII) to Fee Income
pnl_drivers.description: Global payments revenue mix is expected to shift from 46% NII and 54% fee income in 2025 to 44% NII and 56% fee income by 2030. This is driven by easing interest rates dampening net interest margins, while fee-based revenues regain share. DFCs with diversified revenue streams will need to emphasize fee-generating services to maintain profitability.

A sustained 25-basis-point increase in interest rates from 2026 onward could add roughly $100 billion to global revenues by 2030, primarily through higher direct net interest income, offsetting softer transaction volumes. However, over the long term, performance may depend more on the depth of local fee pools and monetization of value-added services.

market_sizing.methodology: McKinsey Global Payments Map analysis of global payments revenues and split by revenue type. Projections are based on current trends in digital transition, financial flows, interest rates, and value-added services. For DFCs, this represents the shifting landscape of their payment-related revenues.
market_sizing.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

pnl_drivers.driver: Margin Compression from Lower Interest Rates
pnl_drivers.description: Lower interest rates in EMEA are compressing treasury and deposit margins for financial institutions, including DFCs, prompting a rapid shift to fee-based structures. This impacts NII profitability, requiring DFCs to focus on fee-generating services.

market_sizing.methodology: McKinsey Global Payments Map projections for regional payment revenue growth in Europe, Middle East, and Africa (EMEA). Relevant for DFCs with operations in Europe.
market_sizing.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

pnl_drivers.description: Agentic AI could put $65 billion of deposit NII at risk by 2030, as software agents automatically sweep idle cash to higher-yielding accounts and investment products, causing balance migration and yield compression for DFCs' banking arms.

Agentic AI could put $10 billion of consumer credit card revenues at risk by 2030, through payment rail substitution, automated repayment optimization, fee avoidance, and real-time foreign-exchange routing, impacting DFCs' card businesses.

market_sizing.methodology: McKinsey's base adoption scenario for agentic AI's impact on global payments revenue, derived from analysis of retail and commercial deposits and consumer credit card revenues. This represents the total revenue at risk for financial institutions globally, impacting DFCs with these business lines.
market_sizing.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

demand_drivers.description: The number of new mortgages in Belgium remained around 10% below the level recorded a year earlier in the first eight months of 2026. This indicates weakening demand for housing finance, directly impacting DFCs involved in mortgage lending.

market_sizing.methodology: ING Think's forecast for nominal median house price increase in Belgium, indicating a cooling trend in the housing market. This acts as a demand driver for mortgage products offered by DFCs with housing finance operations.
market_sizing.source_title: Second-quarter resilience masks a more challenging outlook for Belgian housing

demand_drivers.driver: Increased investment in vertical AI applications
demand_drivers.description: European start-ups focused on vertical AI applications (including financial services) now attract 67% of the funding raised by their US counterparts, up from 9% in 2018. This robust funding signifies a strong ecosystem for specialized AI solutions relevant to DFCs.

new_opportunities.description: Europe's strength in developing vertical AI applications, combined with its regulated environments, presents an opportunity for DFCs to adopt deeply integrated AI solutions to transform complex, everyday business processes in financial services and insurance.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Leveraging specialized AI solutions for complex financial workflows

market_sizing.methodology: McKinsey proprietary funding analysis aggregating data from Dealroom, PitchBook, and Gain, covering venture capital investments in AI applications in Europe. This indicates the investment trend and opportunity for DFCs to adopt or partner with AI solutions.
market_sizing.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity
